title: Little's Law constrains the network
note: Little's Law (L = λW) is the canonical conservation rule for any flow network: the average number of items in the system equals the throughput times the average wait. When throughput saturates, every additional unit of flow becomes wait time, not output — adding capacity is the only response that changes the equilibrium.

title: Cascade propagation
note: Single-node delays propagate to downstream nodes with measurable lag. The propagation pattern is the signature of the network topology — the lag arcs in the system graph make this physical, and the cascade-projection card surfaces which downstream nodes feel the pressure soonest.
